name: SCHOOL_BUS_STOP_YELLOW_DIAMOND

tas_w6-101_bus_child.desc: front of a bus with a child (schoolgirl with a bag) walking at its right, traced from the sheet (black graphics); the same artwork at a smaller size on W6-102 (G/10/445A)

notes: Department of State Growth (formerly DIER) standard drawing, black line-work sheet; every dimension from the sheet unless stated. Series/heights as the sheet's letter-type note; AS 1744 (plus0) spacing, so widths differ from the sheet's figures where its spacing is wider (the TAS sheets' 'medium'/'75%' spacing runs about 7% wider than AS 1744 normal spacing). Sheet G/10/444A 'General school bus stop sign W6-101' (1998, sideways A4): sizes A 600, B 750, C 900, D 1200; drawn at A (600, bounding square 848.53; the companion W6-102 sheet's 50 mm lettering note fits the 600 size), 'black graphics on yellow background'. The sheet draws the diamond as a single outline: no border drawn, so none generated; tip radius not stated, R40 as the AS 1743 600 diamonds. The sheet has no scale: the drawn diamond's rounded extent is taken as the 600 sign's, and the symbol box is its measured extent (bus + child 395 x 371 on the sheet's 848 diamond, i.e. 380 x 356 at 600, top-left 270 / 241). panel_px = the sheet's diamond extent widened by the tip rounding (R40: 16.6 each side) to the sharp bounding square.
